Check that the labels fit inside the canvas

Source: R/fit.R
check_labels_fit.Rd

A subtitle that fits in a preview can still be cut off in the saved figure. This function measures text at the width and height you plan to use.

Usage

check_labels_fit(plot, width = 6.5, height = 4)

Arguments

plot

A ggplot object.

width, height

Intended size in inches. Defaults to 6.5 by 4.

Value

A tibble with one row per element checked: what it needs, what it has, and whether it fits. Invisibly returns the same tibble when all elements fit.

Details

It checks the title, subtitle, caption, axis titles and tick labels on all four sides, legend, and facet strips. If something doesn't fit, try a line break, a wider figure, or a smaller font, then inspect the saved file.

Text inside the panel, including labels from geom_text() and geom_text_last(), isn't measured. Its clipping depends on the panel range and coordinate settings. Check those labels yourself and add room with expansion() where needed. This check can't certify that every label is readable or free of overlap.

Examples

library(ggplot2)
p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg)) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(subtitle = paste(rep("A very long subtitle indeed", 6), collapse = " "))
check_labels_fit(p, width = 6.5, height = 4)
#> Warning: 1 element will be clipped at 6.5in x 4in.
#> ✖ subtitle needs 10.79in but has 5.97in.
#> ℹ Hard-wrap the text, widen the canvas, or reduce the font size.
#> # A tibble: 7 × 4
#>   element                      required_in available_in fits 
#>   <chr>                              <dbl>        <dbl> <lgl>
#> 1 layout (non-panel width)           0.533         6.5  TRUE 
#> 2 layout (non-panel height)          0.724         4    TRUE 
#> 3 subtitle                          10.8           5.97 FALSE
#> 4 x axis title                       0.153         5.97 TRUE 
#> 5 y axis title                       0.292         3.28 TRUE 
#> 6 x axis labels (side by side)       0.278         5.97 TRUE 
#> 7 y axis labels (stacked)            0.583         3.28 TRUE
